questions.q: State the formula for the effective focal length \(F\) of three thin lenses of focal lengths \(f_1, f_2, f_3\) placed in contact. What is the SI unit of the power of this combination?
questions.a: \(\frac{1}{F} = \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2} + \frac{1}{f_3}\); the SI unit of power is dioptre (D), where \(1\,\text{D} = 1\,\text{m}^{-1}\). A wrong answer (e.g., \(F = f_1 + f_2 + f_3\) or unit = watt) reveals confusion between adding focal lengths vs. adding reciprocals, or mixing up power of a lens with electrical power.

questions.q: A convex lens of power +4.0 D and a concave lens of power –2.5 D are placed in contact. A student claims the combination is diverging because "one lens is concave". Explain why this reasoning is incorrect and state the nature of the combination.
questions.a: The net power is \(P = +4.0 + (-2.5) = +1.5\,\text{D}\), which is positive, so the combination is converging. The student's error is assuming the nature is determined by the presence of a concave lens rather than by the algebraic sum of powers. This reveals a misunderstanding that powers add with signs, not that "concave always dominates".

questions.q: Two thin lenses of focal lengths +20 cm and –30 cm are placed in contact. An object is placed 40 cm from the combination. Find the position and nature of the final image. (Use Cartesian sign convention: \(u = -40\,\text{cm}\).)
questions.a: \(f_1 = +20\,\text{cm}, f_2 = -30\,\text{cm}\). \(\frac{1}{F} = \frac{1}{20} + \frac{1}{-30} = \frac{3-2}{60} = \frac{1}{60}\) ⇒ \(F = +60\,\text{cm}\). Lens formula: \(\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{F}\) ⇒ \(\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{60} + \frac{1}{-40} = \frac{2-3}{120} = -\frac{1}{120}\) ⇒ \(v = -120\,\text{cm}\). Image is virtual, erect, on same side as object. A wrong sign in \(u\) or \(F\) leads to a real image at +120 cm — a common sign-convention error.

questions.q: Two combinations are made: (A) a convex lens of focal length 10 cm and a concave lens of focal length 20 cm; (B) two convex lenses each of focal length 20 cm. Compare the effective focal lengths and powers. Which combination has greater converging ability?
questions.a: (A) \(1/F_A = 1/10 + 1/(-20) = 1/20\) ⇒ \(F_A = +20\,\text{cm}, P_A = +5\,\text{D}\). (B) \(1/F_B = 1/20 + 1/20 = 1/10\) ⇒ \(F_B = +10\,\text{cm}, P_B = +10\,\text{D}\). Combination B has greater converging ability (shorter focal length, higher power). A student who says A is stronger because it has a "stronger convex lens" ignores the cancelling effect of the concave lens.

questions.q: A student solves a problem: "Two lenses of powers +3 D and –1 D are in contact. Find the focal length of the combination." Their working: \(P = 3 + 1 = 4\,\text{D}, F = 1/4 = 0.25\,\text{m}\). Identify the error and give the correct answer.
questions.a: The student added the magnitudes instead of the signed powers. Correct: \(P = +3 + (-1) = +2\,\text{D}\), so \(F = 1/2 = 0.5\,\text{m} = 50\,\text{cm}\). The error reveals a failure to treat concave lens power as negative — a sign-convention slip that costs marks in both board and JEE/NEET.

questions.q: Design a combination of two thin lenses in contact that has an effective power of +2.5 D. One lens must be concave. Specify the focal lengths (in cm) of both lenses. (Multiple answers possible; give one valid pair.)
questions.a: Let convex lens power \(P_1 = +5\,\text{D}\) (\(f_1 = +20\,\text{cm}\)), concave lens power \(P_2 = -2.5\,\text{D}\) (\(f_2 = -40\,\text{cm}\)). Then \(P = +5 - 2.5 = +2.5\,\text{D}\). Any pair with \(P_1 + P_2 = +2.5\) and \(P_2 < 0\) works. A poor answer gives both focal lengths positive or ignores the concave requirement, showing inability to work backwards from net power.
